claims.text: High-temperature exposure causes FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings to form an ultrafine protective oxide scale.
The oxide scale is a mixed oxide incorporating Cu, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cr.
The high-temperature oxide scale is self-healing under wear.
Formation of the oxide scale dynamically refines the near-surface microstructure.
The oxide scale acts as a load-bearing and lubricious barrier.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is a uniform nanocrystalline solid solution.
The as-deposited coating has no pre-formed oxide layer.
Exposure in air at 650–900 °C before and during wear testing will induce the proposed oxide scale.
Thermal treatment can alter the wear performance of a high-entropy-alloy coating.
The proposed effect is to be tested during cyclic sliding in air at approximately 650–900 °C.
Thermally activated oxidation rapidly produces a thin, coherent oxide scale.
The oxide layer reduces friction and direct counterface contact.
Reduced direct contact decreases both adhesive and abrasive wear.
FeNiCrCoCu coatings tested at 650–900 °C will have lower wear rates than coatings tested at room temperature.
FeNiCrCoCu coatings tested at 650–900 °C will have a lower coefficient of friction than coatings tested at room temperature.
Post-test microscopy and surface analysis will reveal a continuous ultrafine mixed-oxide layer with evidence of dynamic regeneration.
Room-temperature FeNiCrCoCu coatings without pre-oxidation do not develop the protective oxide layer.
Room-temperature FeNiCrCoCu coatings have higher wear rates and friction than the proposed high-temperature condition.
The beneficial oxide-mediated effect occurs within 650–900 °C but may disappear at lower temperatures because oxidation is insufficient.
At excessively high temperatures, oxide spallation may degrade wear resistance.

contradictions.description: The main comparison is described as high-temperature exposure and testing versus room-temperature testing, but the falsification design says both sets are tested under identical cyclic sliding conditions after only one set is pretreated. It therefore does not consistently specify whether test temperature, pre-oxidation, or both differ between groups.
